title: Period Lengths of Rational Cut-and-Project Gap Sequences
abstract: Formalizes the closed-form minimal periods of one-dimensional rational cut-and-project gap sequences at the level of the paper's residue model, plus a fully geometric aperiodicity theorem for irrational slopes. For coprime α, β ∈ ℕ and window parameter ω ≥ 0, write N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β². The strip-to-residue reduction of the paper — sorting the hits of the length-N progression twisted by the geometric multiplier −αβ⁻¹ (mod D) — is taken as the definition of the gap sequence rather than derived from the lattice; for it, the multiset convention has minimal period N/D when D ∣ N and N otherwise, and the set convention (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 when N ≥ D and N otherwise. The irrational case is geometric from first principles: for positive irrational slope and ω > 0, the accepted points of ℤ² sorted by the physical projection have a gap sequence with no finite period, via injectivity of the projection and Kronecker density of the internal image.

informal.CutAndProject.main_theorem_geometric_con: The gap sequence of the residue model of the rational cut-and-project multiset (sorted hits of the length-N progression under the multiplier −αβ⁻¹ mod D) has minimal period N/D if D divides N and N otherwise, where N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β².
informal.CutAndProject.set_main_theorem_geometric: The set-convention residue-model gap sequence (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 if N ≥ D and N otherwise.
informal.CutAndProject.Irrational.prop_irrational: For positive irrational slope and window parameter ω > 0, the projected gap sequence has no finite period.
